correctness.rationale: The proof gives an elementary equivalence between greedy arch counts and universality, an exact endpoint-run recurrence, and the complete half-open window test. With all run lengths at least two, endpoints advance q-1 run indices per arch. With a singleton, a bounded deficiency variable proves exactly k arches for every phase, including the boundary equality case. The standalone checker passed 9,671 parameter/repetition cases, 105,476 phase-index comparisons and 678 full-spectrum cross-checks; finite tests do not prove the infinite claim.

evidence: Barker et al. (2020) gives universal one-step circular-index bounds and a sufficient circular-gain condition for powers.

broader_coverage.reasoning: These are stronger in generality of input words but weaker in explicit structure for this constrained family: none of the inspected statements identifies the all-phase dichotomy or proves the p-q maximizing-phase count. The present theorem is a new closed-form structural extraction, not a claim of a faster general algorithm.

evidence: For q≥3 the period U itself has iota(U)=zeta(U)=1; therefore Barker et al. Theorem 22, whose premise requires a one-unit circular gain, does not directly give the displayed all-power formula for U.
Theorem 23 of Barker et al. is binary-specific and excluded from the q≥3 scope.
The 2021 general eventual-periodicity theorem specifies existence and a bound, not the exact period q-1 and zero transient in the all-nonsingleton case or the singleton suppression.
The 2023 algorithm computes maximum values for arbitrary input but does not state exact phase multiplicities for all k.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: General algorithms could evaluate each finite instance, and general periodicity results help motivate the proof; neither implication alone subsumes the new formulas and optimizing-phase characterization without doing the family-specific run analysis. This is the remaining distinguishing content.

value.rationale: Subsequence universality and its circular analogue are established invariants. This theorem classifies every cyclic starting position of a full-period power, identifies a sharp singleton-run rigidity threshold, proves a run-length-independent floor law for longer runs, and gives the exact count of optimum phases. Such all-parameter phase spectra and a q-1-period growth law are structural data not supplied by an instance-wise algorithm or general eventual-periodicity bound.
